correctness.rationale: The bidirected K_{3,4} has exactly 24 ordered arcs and its multipath faces are arc subsets with indegree/outdegree <=1 and no directed cycles (including 2-cycles), equivalent to disjoint simple directed paths. An independently written recursive all-arc enumerator found 3301 augmented faces and exactly 144 six-arc facets; an independent explicit subset-size<=6 bounded check in the source code corroborates completeness since 7 vertices prohibit >6 arcs. Reconstructed 1608 augmented toggle matches, all 13104 Hasse covers and full 3301-vertex acyclic ordering, leaving 37 critical 3-cells, 48 4-cells and one 0-cell. Independent *signed integer* Morse projection computed the entire 37x48 matrix and found every entry zero; the Hurewicz isomorphism pi3(vee^37 S3)=Z37 gives 37 S3 +48 S4. Pure dimension-five with H3 and H4 nonzero is not shellable. The finite proof applies precisely to this digraph, not every bidirected K_{m,n}.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial complete bipartite bidirected case K3,4 beyond one-way chessboard matchings supplies a natural missing arc-cycle-containing multipath invariant. Its two adjacent nonzero homotopy degrees, exact primitive integral attachments and purity/non-shellability tension are meaningful relative to published acyclic bipartite Euler-count formulas and bidirected path/polygon or double-star families; future comparisons of more general bidirected multipartite complexes can use this precise benchmark without a general-family theorem.

limitations: Unindexed bidirected complete-bipartite multipath calculations might have been published under path-poset or cycle-free chessboard terminology.
